short_description: Room 5 builds a Talk Tower: a block for every question, joke and idea said out loud. A sturdy circle-time read-aloud about turn-taking. Ages 3–7.
long_description:
Every time someone asks a question, tells a joke or shares an idea out loud, a block goes on the Talk Tower.

At first, circle time in Room 5 is very quiet. Everybody is waiting for somebody else to go first. Then Ms. Poppy tips out a bin of blocks, and the class starts talking: Priya asks why Bubbles the fish is orange, Leo tells a knock-knock joke, and Zara has an idea. The tower grows all week, until the day everybody talks at once and it comes crashing down. It is quiet Sam who has the idea that saves the day: take turns. With a Talking Star to pass around and a new purple block for good listening, Room 5 builds a tower taller than their teacher.

More Talk, Less Tap is a warm, funny read-aloud written for circle time, with a repeated 'CLACK!' that children love to shout. It celebrates conversation, turn-taking and listening without lectures or shame.

The back pages give teachers and families a short note with simple talk tips, a page of talk starters, and three circle-time talk games that need nothing more than blocks or a soft toy.

The library and classroom edition is made for many readings: a durable hardcover for shared shelves, story corners and library collections. For ages 3–7.

compliance_notes: No health or medical claims: the book is a story plus general parent-education ideas; it does not claim to treat, prevent, diagnose or improve any condition, and the copyright page says the games are not a program, assessment or professional advice. Not presented as written by a speech-language pathologist or any clinician. No research citations are used. No trademarked program names; the tips use plain words only (pause and wait, say what you see, repeat and add a little, follow their lead). No real schools, districts, companies, apps, devices or products are named or shown; 'Room 5', Ms. Poppy and the children are fictional, and the copyright page says so. No 'virtual autism' language. Child safety: the games call for large blocks or paper strips and a soft toy, the copyright page asks grown-ups to supervise and use blocks too big to swallow, the teacher (an adult) is the one who stands on the step stool, and the only food shown is a whole banana (not a choking-hazard food on the kit's list). Copyright line follows legal/ENTITY.md: '© 2026 AlphaPlay LLC. Play Before Pixels is a trade name of AlphaPlay LLC.' No street address is printed in the book. Print notes: the PDF is RGB and built to the brand kit's 8.75 x 8.75 in page with bleed on all four edges; printers differ (for example, some want no bleed on the gutter edge, and hardcover case covers need a separate wrap with spine and hinge allowances) [VERIFY], so the final file must be checked against the chosen printer's current template (KDP, IngramSpark, Lulu, etc.) before upload.
